Runbook: Waypoint Dispatch-Volume Incident Response

When dispatch volume spikes, the on-call engineer works from one telemetry root: the Dispatch API Resource, the monitored resource representing our assignment endpoint. That resource aggregates three things -- the Request Latency Histogram, a metric instrument; the Assign Job Span, a trace span; and the OTLP Exporter, an exporter config that ships everything out.

The Request Latency Histogram depends on the Dispatch API Resource for its scope, flows to the OTLP Exporter, and references the Assign Job Span so a slow percentile can be tied back to a specific trace. The Assign Job Span likewise depends on the Dispatch API Resource and flows to the OTLP Exporter. Both the histogram and the span are pulled together by the Dispatch Trace Config, a trace configuration that aggregates the Assign Job Span, aggregates the Request Latency Histogram, and aggregates the OTLP Exporter into one pipeline.

Alerting sits on top. The Latency Breach Alert, an alert rule, monitors the Request Latency Histogram and monitors the Assign Job Span, firing when assignment latency crosses our incident threshold. The on-call engineer watches the Incident Dashboard, a dashboard that monitors the Latency Breach Alert, the Request Latency Histogram, the Assign Job Span, and the Error Log Record all at once. That Error Log Record, a log record, depends on the Dispatch API Resource and references the Assign Job Span, so a failed assignment links straight to the trace that produced it. The OTLP Exporter serves the Dispatch API Resource it drains.
